findings.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28 — `unsubscribe` is gated by `ensure_logged_in` yet is the target of an email link; a recipient who is not logged in in that browser (the common email-click case) hits Discourse::NotLoggedIn on a GET html request and gets the not-found page instead of an unsubscribe, and there is no signed key (cf. the existing `DigestUnsubscribeKey` pattern used by the digest email) so the feature does not work for the population it was built for (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:104 — `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` followed by `tu.notification_level` assumes a topic_users row exists; the URL is guessable/shareable and any logged-in user opening `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic they have never been emailed about (no row) gets `undefined method 'notification_level' for nil` — the model already provides the upsert-by-design `TopicUser.change` and the controller bypasses it (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:106-112 — writing `tu.notification_level` + `tu.save!` directly instead of `TopicUser.change(..., notification_level:)` leaves `notifications_reason_id` nil and `notifications_changed_at` unset, so the row is still treated as "never explicitly changed by the user": `TopicUser.auto_track` (guarded by `notifications_reason_id: nil`) and the `update_last_read` SQL (`case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and total_msecs_viewed > threshold then :tracking`) will silently flip a just-muted user back to tracking the next time they reply to or read the topic, and no `MessageBus.publish(notification_level_change)` is sent so open tabs show the stale level (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:106-110 — the GET action is a two-step ratchet, not an idempotent unsubscribe: `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted`; a watching user who clicks the link (-> regular), then refreshes/re-opens the page or clicks the link in the next email they still receive at regular (replies/mentions/quotes still email at regular) is silently pushed to muted, while the page text claims "You will stop receiving notifications" after the first click when it did not (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855 — the shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now hard-requires `%{unsubscribe_url}` but `Email::MessageBuilder` only gates on `add_unsubscribe_link` and never defaults `unsubscribe_url`; any caller (plugin or future mailer) passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without the new key raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at send time in both `body` (lib/email/message_builder.rb:90) and `html_part` (lib/email/message_builder.rb:67), and the spec masks this by always supplying the key (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:99,115 — the unsubscribe action instantiates a full `TopicView` (posts, filters) and then `perform_show_response` serializes the whole `TopicViewSerializer` into `store_preloaded`, while the Ember `topicUnsubscribe` route (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-6) ignores that preload and refetches the topic view via `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` just to show a title and a notification dropdown; deleting `perform_show_response` in favour of rendering the bare app shell (or a small JSON with slug/title/notification_level) removes one full topic serialization per click and the duplicate fetch (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/app-route-map.js.es6:13 — the client route `topicUnsubscribe` `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` performs no state change; only the server-side full-page GET mutates, so any in-app navigation to this URL (Discourse.URL intercepts `/t/` links for client-side transitions, browser back/forward into the route) renders "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>" without anything having changed — the mutation and the confirmation UI live in different layers with no shared contract (severity P2, confidence 50, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:106 — one click from watching/tracking only drops to `regular` (`tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`), and per config/locales/client.en.yml:1081 regular still means "You will be notified if someone mentions your @name or replies to you", so the footer promise in config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 ("To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic") is false for user_replied/user_mentioned/user_quoted and for user_private_message (PM participants are watching by default); the recipient keeps getting the exact email type they clicked to stop (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:8 — `ensure_logged_in` on `:unsubscribe` with no return-to handling means a logged-out recipient (the common case for links opened from a mail client) hits Discourse::NotLoggedIn, which ApplicationController renders as an HTML 404 for non-XHR GETs, so the anonymous/logged-out acceptance case is unhandled: no login redirect, no post-login return to the unsubscribe URL (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:104 — `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is nil for the wrong-user case (a logged-in user who opens a forwarded/shared unsubscribe link for a topic they have no topic_users row for) and line 106 then raises NoMethodError on `tu.notification_level`, returning a 500 instead of a no-op or message (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:112 — `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change` (app/models/topic_user.rb:84-87), so the sibling columns `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) are never set and no `notification_level_change` MessageBus publish fires; the stale reason is why the client resorts to `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)` in routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:14, and open topic tabs keep showing the old level (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:106 — the action toggles rather than unsubscribes: the already-unsubscribed state is unhandled, so a second GET of the same emailed link (re-opening the mail, Outlook SafeLinks/mail-scanner prefetch, browser link prefetch) escalates regular -> muted silently while the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications"; a state-changing GET with no idempotency guard is the trigger (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — the only spec change adds `unsubscribe_url:` to a fixture; there is no test that `body`/`html_part` contain the topic unsubscribe URL, none for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, and none for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (toggle semantics, slug redirect, login requirement, nil topic_user), so the new behaviour is unverified (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:145 — `mailing_list_notify` also flows through `send_notification_email` and now carries the per-topic link, but the link only mutes the TopicUser row; unless Jobs::NotifyMailingListSubscribers excludes muted topics (not verifiable in this snapshot) mailing-list-mode users keep receiving every post after clicking "stop receiving notifications" (severity P2, confidence 50, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — the Ember route only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (GET /t/:id.json) and never hits `topics#unsubscribe`, so any client-side transition to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe (internal link in a post routed via Discourse.URL, back/forward navigation) renders "You will stop receiving notifications" without changing the notification level; web route and JS route disagree on who performs the side effect (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 — `unsubscribe_link` now hard-requires `%{unsubscribe_url}` but `Email::MessageBuilder` supplies no default for it, so any other `add_unsubscribe_link: true` caller (plugin mailers, future core mailers) raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at send time; the fixture edit in message_builder_spec.rb:172 is the symptom of this new implicit contract (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil for any user with no topic_users row (e.g. mentioned/quoted in a topic they never visited, which is exactly who gets notification emails), so `tu.notification_level` at line 107 raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe writes nothing; the replaced `TopicUser.change` upsert path created the row in this case, so the new path silently loses the mute for a whole class of recipients (severity P1, confidence 100, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-113 — writing `tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which is the only path that stamps `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (`||= notification_reasons[:user_changed]`, app/models/topic_user.rb:88-89); with `notifications_reason_id` left NULL, `update_last_read` (topic_user.rb:161 `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and (tu.total_msecs_viewed + :msecs) > coalesce(...)`) and `auto_track` (topic_user.rb:38 `notifications_reason_id: nil`) treat the row as never user-touched and re-promote it to tracking on the very next read past the auto-track threshold — the action itself renders the topic page so the client starts reporting read time immediately, meaning the mute/regular the user just chose is silently reverted, and `notifications_changed_at` stays stale for anything that reads it (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-113 — the direct `save!` path omits the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })` that `TopicUser.change` emits (topic_user.rb:114), so any other open tab of the topic for that user keeps displaying the pre-unsubscribe level and its dropdown writes back the stale value on next interaction, undoing the unsubscribe (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-111 — the email promises "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" (server.en.yml unsubscribe_link) but for watching/tracking rows the code writes `notification_levels[:regular]` (still emailed on replies-to-you/mentions/quotes), while a second click on the same link from a later email flips regular -> muted; the written enum value drifts from what the email text tells the user and the link is a stepper rather than an idempotent unsubscribe, so a user who clicks twice ends up muted without asking for it (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is dereferenced unguarded at line 107 (`tu.notification_level > ...`), so any logged-in user hitting `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` for a topic with no topic_users row (hand-typed/forwarded link, topic never visited or emailed) gets NoMethodError on nil -> HTTP 500 instead of a muted/regular state (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

lib/email/message_builder.rb:90 — `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml:1852) but the interpolation is only supplied by `send_notification_email` (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:295); any other MessageBuilder caller passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` (the pre-change spec at spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:169 is exactly that shape and had to be patched) raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at send time (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-111 — the state change is performed on an idempotency-free GET with toggle semantics (`> regular` -> regular, else -> muted), so a user who lands from the email (watching -> regular) and then refreshes the page or clicks the same email link again is silently escalated to muted, which the Ember page text does not reflect (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:111 — `tu.save!` writes notification_level directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change` (app/models/topic_user.rb:77), so `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` are not stamped and no `/topic/:id` MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published; other open tabs on that topic keep showing the old level and the reason text stays stale for this user (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` mutes/downgrades whoever is logged in the browser, not the email recipient: the mailed link (`post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, no signed key, unlike the existing digest flow's DigestUnsubscribeKey with its `different_user_description` guard at config/locales/server.en.yml:555) sends a logged-out recipient to the `ensure_logged_in` wall (line 28) so the unsubscribe never happens, and on a shared/other-account session it silently changes the other account's notification level for that topic (severity P1, confidence 100, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted` on a GET makes the unsubscribe link non-idempotent: a watching user who clicks once gets regular, then a browser refresh, back-navigation, or a second click on the same email link (or any later email for the topic, all of which carry the identical URL) escalates them to muted with no confirmation, while the page copy still reads as a single "stop notifications" action (severity P2, confidence 100, blocking)

config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 — the email promises "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here]" and client.en.yml:986 confirms "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}", but for the main audience of these emails (watchers receiving `user_posted`) the code at topics_controller.rb:108 sets `notification_levels[:regular]`, so the recipient keeps receiving reply/mention/quote notification emails for that topic after being told they were unsubscribed (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — `tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, so unlike every other notification-level change in the model (app/models/topic_user.rb:113,194,218) no `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is published and `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id` stay stale; a user with the topic open in another tab keeps seeing "Watching" and the stale "you will receive notifications because..." reason after unsubscribing (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — the Ember `topicUnsubscribe` route only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (`/t/:id.json`) and never hits `topics#unsubscribe`, so any client-side transition to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (browser back after the initial load, in-app link) renders "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}" without changing anything server-side (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:103 — `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil for any logged-in user without a topic_users row (email link opened while logged in as a different account than the recipient, or /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe typed for a never-visited topic) and `tu.notification_level` at :105 raises NoMethodError, producing a raw 500 where a create-or-update (TopicUser.change) or 4xx belongs (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-111 — the action sets `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!`s without stamping `notifications_reason_id` (TopicUser.change stamps :user_changed at topic_user.rb:88), so rows whose reason is nil — exactly the rows the mailer creates via `TopicUser.change(user.id, post.topic_id, last_emailed_post_number: ...)` at app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:312 — stay reason-nil and `update_last_read` (topic_user.rb:159-167 `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null ... then :tracking`) / `auto_track` (topic_user.rb:38) silently flip the muted user back to :tracking the next time they read or interact with the topic; the unsubscribe is undone with no signal to anyone (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-109 + app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 — the confirmation page unconditionally renders "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>" but a :watching/:tracking user is only lowered to :regular (`tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`), a level that still emails on replies/mentions/quotes, so the page reports a completed unsubscribe that did not happen while the adjacent `topic-notifications-button` shows "Normal", contradicting the text (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

lib/email/message_builder.rb:67,88 + config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`; any `Email::MessageBuilder` caller (core, plugin, or future) passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `:unsubscribe_url` raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument inside `body`/`html_part` and the email is never built — the spec at spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 had to be patched to add `unsubscribe_url` precisely because of this raise (severity P2, confidence 50, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:8-28,99 — `ensure_logged_in` on a non-XHR HTML GET is rescued by ApplicationController as a 404 not-found page, so a logged-out email recipient clicking "click here" gets "Page Not Found" with no login redirect and no mutation, whereas the existing `/my/preferences` unsubscribe link redirects to login and returns (severity P2, confidence 50, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:111 — `tu.save!` bypasses the `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... })` that `TopicUser.change` performs at topic_user.rb:113, so any other open tab on the topic keeps displaying the pre-unsubscribe level until reload (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:99-111 — the mutation runs on every GET of the confirmation URL, so a browser refresh (F5) or back/forward re-lowers the level (watching -> regular -> muted) without any new user intent; a watching user who reloads once ends up muted rather than at the level the page told them about (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:102 — the slug-mismatch branch does `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301` without appending `.json` (unlike `redirect_to_correct_topic` at :454), so a JSON client with a stale slug follows the 301 into the HTML `show` page (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` has no rejection handler and the route defines no `error` action, so a failed follow-up `/t/:id.json` fetch (transient network/5xx) leaves the user on a blank page with no indication that the server already mutated their notification level in the preceding request (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, so every `Email::MessageBuilder` caller passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without an `unsubscribe_url` (any plugin or non-post mailer) raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at send time; the diff hides this by editing spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 to supply the new arg instead of keeping the existing contract (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — the email promises "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" but `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted` only steps a watching/tracking user down to regular, where user_replied/user_mentioned/user_quoted emails (the very emails carrying the link) keep arriving; the stated intent is only met on a second click, and client.en.yml:985 tells the user they have stopped receiving notifications when they have not (severity P2, confidence 75, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28 — `:unsubscribe` is behind `ensure_logged_in` with no token/one-click path, so a recipient who clicks the email link from a mail client without an active browser session hits the NotLoggedIn rescue page rather than an unsubscribe flow; the feature "unsubscribe option in emails" only works for already-logged-in users (severity P2, confidence 50, blocking)

app/models/topic_user.rb:8 — six hunks in this file (scope indentation, create_lookup, MessageBus.publish hash spacing, track_visit! hash braces) are whitespace-only reformatting with no call from the feature; unrelated churn in a core model that inflates the diff and blame for a change that never needed to touch it (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6:11 — the whole file is rewritten (function->method shorthand, var->const, `self` hoisted into the const block, blank-line shuffles) yet nothing in the feature calls or depends on this route; it is an untraceable drive-by refactor of the main topic-loading route bundled into an email feature (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

app/views/email/notification.html.erb:3 — the template is fully re-indented and converted to `render partial:` syntax while the only placeholder the feature relies on (`%{unsubscribe_link}`) already existed unchanged; zero feature-related lines in a 40-line rewrite of the email body template (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

lib/email/message_builder.rb:24 — every hunk here (template_args hash layout, respond_instructions assignment shape, html_part blank lines, gsub spacing) is cosmetic; the feature flows entirely through the pre-existing `.merge!(@opts)`, so this file did not need to change and the rewrite obscures that no behavioural change was made (severity P3, confidence 100, advisory)

config/routes.rb:439 — the `summary` routes lose their `post_number: /\d+/` constraint and `moderator-liked` is reordered, neither of which is needed to add the two `unsubscribe` routes; unrelated route edits in a feature commit (severity P3, confidence 75, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/components/dropdown-button.js.es6:28 — making `title` optional alters rendering for every DropdownButton consumer, but the unsubscribe page uses `topic-notifications-button`, which sets its own title, so the `<h4>` still renders there and this change has no observable effect on the feature it is bundled with (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — the only spec touched is the one adjusted to absorb the contract change; no spec covers `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `Topic#unsubscribe_url`, the new routes, or that notification emails now carry the per-topic link, so a regression in any of them ships silently (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — `def unsubscribe` is routed as `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb:440-441) and mutates `tu.notification_level` + `tu.save!` on a plain GET with no signed token and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` (line 32) removing the only non-XHR guard; Rails forgery protection never runs on GET, so an attacker embedding `` on any page (or any link-prefetching browser/mail client carrying the victim's session cookie) silently demotes the logged-in victim's watching/tracking level on topic 123 to regular and, on a second hit, to muted — CSRF state change (severity P1, confidence 100, blocking)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is dereferenced unconditionally at line 107 (`tu.notification_level > ...`), so any logged-in user opening an unsubscribe URL for a topic they have no topic_users row for (forwarded email link, guessed id) gets a NoMethodError 500 instead of a handled response (severity P2, confidence 100, advisory)

lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (also line 89) now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}` because the server.en.yml:1852 string interpolates it, but MessageBuilder never defaults it; any caller passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` (plugins, the digest/mailing-list paths if they adopt the flag) raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and the email job aborts — the spec at spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 had to be patched to hide exactly this (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 — `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` triple-stashes the client `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })` output; client I18n does not escape interpolations, so the only thing standing between a topic title like `` and stored XSS is the server-side `ERB::Util.html_escape(title)` in app/models/topic.rb:264 — the template should use a double-stash with the strong tag moved out of the locale string rather than relying on that invariant (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — The only test edit in the diff injects `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` into the `let` while neither `it` in the context asserts that value appears anywhere (line 179 still only matches `user_preferences_url`); the key was added solely because `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (lib/email/message_builder.rb:66 and :91) now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` and raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` without it, so the spec masks that regression (any `add_unsubscribe_link: true` builder without `unsubscribe_url`, e.g. a plugin mailer, now blows up at send time) instead of proving the per-topic link is rendered into the body (severity P1, confidence 75, blocking)

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:175 — `expect(...header_args['List-Unsubscribe']).to be_present` is a false-confidence assertion: the header is still `<#{user_preferences_url}>` (lib/email/message_builder.rb:107) and never carries the new per-topic URL, so this test passes identically whether or not the feature touches headers and a reviewer reading "has an List-Unsubscribe header" under a per-topic-unsubscribe diff is misled about what is covered (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:154 — No example in the spec passes `html_override`, so `html_part` (lib/email/message_builder.rb:58-70) — the only code path that substitutes `%{unsubscribe_link}` into the HTML notification body that app/views/email/notification.html.erb was restructured around, and whose output changed from one paragraph to two via the new `unsubscribe_link: |` block literal cooked by PrettyText — has zero coverage; a regression in the gsub or in PrettyText rendering of the two-line link ships silently to every HTML notification email (severity P2, confidence 75, advisory)

spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — The stub `"/t/1234/unsubscribe"` is a relative path while the production value `Topic#unsubscribe_url` (app/models/topic.rb:719) is absolute (`Discourse.base_url`-prefixed); because the stub carries no host, a future assertion written against it cannot catch the mailer passing a relative URL that renders as a dead link in the recipient's mail client (severity P3, confidence 50, advisory)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route/action `topics#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb; app/controllers/topics_controller.rb) and injects `unsubscribe_url` into notification emails (user_notifications.rb; server.en.yml).
